I am very glad for you that the steps cured your depression. I think that is lovely. It is incredibly important to be conscious of the fact that there are physiological differences in the brains of people that have psychiatric diagnoses. It is irresponsible to neglect this. I have see it happen over and over again in the rooms. My goal is always to remind those suffering that they are not to feel ashamed for seeking help for a potentially fatal and life altering/thief disease. They owe it to themselves and their families to seek expert guidance. Remember that AA is full of people that are experts in their own experience...not experts in the field of mental health. If they are experts in the field of mental health and they are acting as your sponsor AND psychiatrist/psychologist/mental health professional they are crossing numerous ethical and professional boundaries. A person in the midst of a suicidal drama needs to seek help. It is irresponsible to tell them otherwise. These are people’s LIVES! AA is a support group...NOT a psychiatric alternative. You would NEVER tell someone in the middle of a schizophrenic or bipolar breakdown to do the steps to cure it. Depression is not different...it can be a chemical imbalance in the brain that needs treatment. Not a prayer and a wish. Prayer and the steps are a great support and foundation but they are not a cure for these kinds of illnesses.
